status: pre-registered-design (Phase C-design); fixed before any remote result
authority: Network profiles are NOT restated here: they are read from research/methods/thresholds.json protocol.network_profiles (decision-method.md section 4.15, Appendix C.1). The latency model parameters mss_bytes and initial_window_rule are read from thresholds.json protocol.latency_model. This file adds only what section 4.15 requires each experiment family to declare: the connection models, the slow-start sensitivity arms (harness review R1-14), header-byte accounting and the exact request-latency algorithm.

CM-H1-TLS-KA.role: primary for every remote experiment in the remote domain
CM-H1-TLS-KA.tls: TLS 1.3 full handshake, modelled (the emulator performs no TLS; setup cost is a sleep of setup_rtts x RTT, ebr-netem-proxy --setup-rtt-multiple 2.0)
CM-H1-TLS-KA.connection_reuse: one persistent connection per session, serial requests (production reqwest blocking client, crates/entrybound/src/random_access.rs:196-203)
CM-H1-TLS-KA.rationale: Matches what the production HttpRangeSource does against an https URL: one pooled keep-alive connection, requests issued one at a time, HEAD for revision checks. [FORMALLY_DERIVED from the cited code; TLS 1.3 = 1 extra RTT is EXTERNALLY_SOURCED: RFC 8446 section 2 full handshake]

CM-H1-PLAIN-KA.connection_reuse: one persistent connection per session, serial

CM-H1-TLS-FRESH.role: sensitivity arm: intermediaries that close the connection after every response
CM-H1-TLS-FRESH.tls: TLS 1.3 full handshake per connection, modelled
CM-H1-TLS-FRESH.connection_reuse: none: a new connection (setup + fresh cwnd) for every request

CM-H1-TLS-N.role: EXP-REMOTE-006 only: N parallel persistent HTTP/1.1 connections sharing one bottleneck link
CM-H1-TLS-N.connection_reuse: N persistent connections, one request in flight per connection
CM-H1-TLS-N.link_sharing: fluid max-min fair split of the profile bandwidth among connections with bytes in flight; each connection keeps its own cwnd

CM-H2-TLS.http_version: HTTP/2 (emulated over prior-knowledge h2c; TLS modelled)
CM-H2-TLS.connection_reuse: one connection, up to S concurrent streams, S in {4, 16, 100}
CM-H2-TLS.link_sharing: all streams share one cwnd; no loss so no TCP head-of-line blocking is modelled

SS-RFC6928.growth: cwnd doubles after every flight that is followed by another flight; no loss
SS-RFC6928.idle_restart: never (cwnd persists across requests on a reused connection)

SS-IDLE-RESET.role: sensitivity arm [INFERRED approximation of RFC 5681 section 4.1 restart after idle and Linux net.ipv4.tcp_slow_start_after_idle=1, which the WSL environment reports]
SS-IDLE-RESET.idle_restart: before a request whose preceding client idle gap exceeds rto_idle_s = 0.2 + rtt_s, cwnd = min(cwnd, initial window)

SS-NONE.role: sensitivity arm; physics of the application-level emulator (harness review R1-14)
SS-NONE.growth: none: every response is paced at the link rate immediately

SS-IW4.role: sensitivity arm: conservative initial window [EXTERNALLY_SOURCED: RFC 3390 section 1, min(4*MSS, max(2*MSS, 4380 bytes))]

byte_accounting.http_bytes: sum over responses of (response body bytes + response header bytes); objective M12.2
byte_accounting.response_header_bytes: measured per response by the origin (ebr-origin --log field header_bytes, tooling T3); for model-only strategies without an origin run, the per-(server, status, method) median measured in EXP-REMOTE-001 probe P5 is used and the substitution is labelled

pseudocode: for each request r in issue order:
if cwnd is null or connection_reuse == none: T += setup_rtts_per_connection * rtt_s; cwnd = IW
else if arm == SS-IDLE-RESET and r.client_gap_before_s > 0.2 + rtt_s: cwnd = min(cwnd, IW)
if arm == SS-NONE: T += 8 * B / bw_bps
if cwnd >= bdp: T += 8 * remaining / bw_bps; remaining = 0
if remaining > 0: T += rtt_s; cwnd = 2 * cwnd
operation latency = sum of latency(r) over the operation's requests (client CPU time excluded and reported separately)
task latency = sum over the task's operations of operation latency + declared client gaps
request_latency_algorithm.implementations: Two independent implementations must agree: Rust ebr_netem::model (tooling T2) and Python research/tools/remote/latency_model.py (tooling T2). Acceptance: identical results within 1e-9 s on 10,000 seeded request sequences per (profile, connection model, arm) before any use.
request_latency_algorithm.tag: FORMALLY_DERIVED given the declared model; the model's fidelity to real TCP is the subject of EXP-REMOTE-001 arm A3 and EXP-REMOTE-013

workload_client_gaps.note: Gap inserted between operations of a task (never between requests of one operation). Only SS-IDLE-RESET is sensitive to it.

decision_robustness_rule: A remote-domain selection made under SS-RFC6928 is labelled slow_start_robust only if the same candidate is the R8 winner (or a member of the R10 tie set) under SS-NONE and SS-IDLE-RESET in every evaluation condition of its scope. Otherwise the record carries slow_start_dependent, naming the arm and condition; such a selection cannot become DECIDED until the kernel-TCP arm (EXP-REMOTE-001 A3) or a real path (EXP-REMOTE-013) reproduces the direction. This implements harness review round 1 use constraint 7 and adds no threshold.
